title: Stay cool and safe: El Paso officials share heat safety tips - NewsBreak
text:
By Jocelyn Flores No media credit provided. ,
1 hours ago
EL PASO, Texas ( KTSM ) — The El Paso Fire Department and the Office of Emergency Management are providing El Pasoans tips on how to be safe and cool during these scorching days.
“Try to limit outdoor activity to the cooler times of the day. If you are going to be outside, wear lighter clothing and hydrate. If you’re feeling thirsty, thirst can be a late sign of dehydration,” Matthew Hunter, captain with the El Paso Fire Department and assistant emergency management coordinator for the El Paso City-County, said.
Hunter also encourages using cooling centers for refugees from the heat. The City and OEM activated the centers this week due to the rising triple-digit temperatures.
City of El Paso activates cooling centers as triple-digit heat lingers all week He also mentioned the symptoms to keep an eye out for heat exhaustion.
“If you’re getting heat and exhaustion, you’re going to feel fatigued. You’re going to have excessive sweatiness, possibly dizzy and nausea,” Hunter said.
These heat safety tips apply not only to humans but also to pets. Hunter advises pet owners to keep their pets off sidewalks, as the surfaces can burn their feet.
“The concrete gets really hot in the summer, so if you’re going to walk your dogs, do it early in the morning or the cooler hours. We don’t want to burn their feet on the sidewalk or asphalt,” he said.
Lastly, Hunter advises residents to use the “buddy system” for individuals, such as the elderly, children or anyone who lives along, to check up on them during this time of year.
“If you have any friends, family, relatives who live alone, let’s check on them. Never leave a child, pet, or elderly person in a car alone. And if you do see a child, pet, or elderly person in a vehicle, call 911,” he said.
